name: 11 Leonis Minoris
description: A naked-eye star 11.4 parsecs away, the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82885: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.821 +/- 0.013 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.003 +/- 0.016

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82885: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 0.91 +/- 0.02

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82885: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5434 +/- 45

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 82885: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 87.96 +/- 0.32 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 11 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.821 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.003 solar radii and 5,434 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 82885: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
